blocks.value: RF and Microwave Engineering courses basically deals with the wireless communications, radars and navigation, medical imaging and radio science . RF and Microwave Engineering falls under the umbrella of Electrical Engineering, with a strong focus on the analytical study and usage of electromagnetic waves and frequencies used to operate various devices, machinery, and systems . In India the RF and Microwave Engineering is mostly given as a specialization at the PG level after completing a UG degree in Electronics and Communication Engineering and Electrical Engineering, or another relevant field.

Why Pursue RF & Microwave Engineering?

Studying RF and Microwave Engineering can prove to be extremely beneficial for students in the digitalized world that we are living in today, where everything around us is operated electronically with the help of electromagnetic waves and signals. Some of the benefits of pusuing RF and Microwave Engineering are mentioned below:

Diverse Career Options: RF Microwave engineers are in demand across various industries such as aerospace, defense, medical devices, telecommunications, and consumer electronics. RF and microwave engineers can be found figuring out the best way to securely encode a signal for transmission and implementing the circuitry to do so. For example, a radio station takes the audio signal of some song, modulate it by encoding it as a high frequency which is ready to travel through the air. It is then received by the radio in our bedroom for us to hear it clearly and enjoy.

Skill Enhancement: RF Microwave engineers can also be found assisting the medical field, for instance, with MRI machines. MRI machines use radio frequency pulses and magnetic fields to generate detailed images of the internal structures of the body, giving medical professionals invaluable insights on their patients. All of this leads to an excellent growth in terms of skills and technical expertise in such an intricate domain.

Earning Potential: The earning opportunities for RF Microwave engineers are quite decent because of the complex tasks that they accomplish and their demand across industries. Recruiters often pay them well. For people interested in electromagnetic waves zooming through space or enhancing the lives of medical patients, RF and microwave engineering could be the profession for them.

faqs.question: What is RF and Microwave Engineering?
faqs.answer: RF & Microwave Engineering is a sub-branch that includes transmission or receiving a radio wave on all devices under radiofrequency . RF (Radio Frequency) & Microwave Engineering is a subset of electrical engineering. These specialists design, construct and operate devices that transmit or receive radio waves. These devices include radios, wireless equipment, mobile phones etc. An RF (Radio Frequency) & Microwave Engineering programme is most suitable for individuals wanting to develop their expertise and grow in the field of  RF, microwave, millimetre wave engineering.

faqs.question: Who can pursue RF and Microwave Engineering courses?
faqs.answer: RF and Microwave Engineering courses are offered at the undergraduate and postgraduate levels. If you have completed your Class 12 in Science background and have studied Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics as compulsory subjects, you are eligible to pursue RF and Microwave Engineering course. You can also take up a UG level course in Electronics and Communication Engineering or Electrical Engineering , and then opt for M.Tech RF and Microwave Engineering as only 4 colleges in India offer a full-fledged course in this field at the undergraduate level. Further, for taking up the course at the postgraduate level, you should have completed BTech degree or BE in ECE/Electrical Engineering, or any other allied discipline and must also possess a valid GATE score. Entrance tests are an important part of the admission process for which you need to work hard and get good marks to secure admission at prestigious Engineering institutions in the country.

faqs.question: Can I pursue RF and Microwave Engineering courses with PCB subjects in Class 12?
faqs.answer: You cannot opt for courses in RF and Microwave Engineering with PCB stream in Class 12. The academic institutions require you to have studied Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics subjects in Class 12 and secured at least 50% marks in your board exams to be eligible for RF and Microwave Engineering courses. It is important to note that out of the 33 RF and Microwave Engineering colleges in India, only 4 colleges provide the courses at the UG-level. Rest, all of the colleges offer MTech courses in RF & Microwave Engineering for which you must have a BTech degree in ECE or Electrical Engineering with at least 55 to 60% marks and a valid entrance exam score like GATE or CUET PG. syllabus.title: RF & Microwave Engineering Syllabus 2025: Check Semester-wise Subjects & Syllabus

blocks.value: A sub-branch in the field of Electronics and Communications Engineering, Radio Frequency(RF) and Microwave Engineering deals with the designing, construction and operation of devices instrumental in transmitting or receiving radio and micro waves. An important aspect of our day to day life, RF and Microwave Engineering finds its application from mobile phone to Bluetooth to Wi-Fi as well as Radar systems and Satellite communication. With advancements in communication technology and application of 3G, 4G and the newly launched 5G systems, RF and Microwave Engineering is an important field of study under Electronics and Communications Engineering.

This course is offered as a specialisation in Master of Technology under the department of Electronics and Communications Engineering across popular engineering colleges in India. It prepares candidates to design and conduct independent research in Microwave communications and construct Smart Antennas for smooth communication. Professionals trained in this course are highly required in Space Research Organisations and Meteorology Departments who deal with satellite communication for their work.

The course structure of M.Tech in RF and Microwave Engineering is similar to M.Tech Radar and Microwave Engineering as well as M.Tech in Microwave Engineering. It provides wide range of opportunities to professionals who are trained in using modern engineering tools to design circuits and assemble satellite arrays.
Important Facts- RF and Microwave Engineering

value: Eligibility Criteria - Candidates aspiring to pursue M.Tech in RF and Microwave Engineering must have completed B.Tech in Electronics and Communication Engineering from a recognised university. They must have cleared national-level or state-level entrance exams for admissions to postgraduate courses.
Course Fees - Government colleges have an average fee structure of INR 50,000- INR 2 lakh per annum, whereas private colleges have an average fee structure of INR 1 lakh- INR 3 lakh per annum.

Learning Outcomes - Candidates after completing this specialised course shall be able to conduct their independent research on RF and Microwave technology, design circuits and create array and circuit models using computer software. They will learn about the application of Advanced Satellite and Mobile Communication and Advanced Electromagnetism in the field of RF and Microwave Engineering

Scope and Career Opportunities - This course provides diverse career opportunities, wherein professionals can work in various multinational telecommunication companies such as Nokia, Qualcomm, Verizon or space research organisations such as SpaceX, ISRO, NASA etc. They can work as Electrical Engineers, RF Engineers, Research and Development Engineer and Design Engineer.

Syllabus for RF and Microwave Engineering

value: The course introduces to the material properties of semiconductors, applications of microwave transistors and diodes and functioning of transferred electron devices and transit-time devices.
Learners understand the design of aperture antennas which are used for wireless communication, characteristics of dielectric resonator antenna and smart antennas.
This course deals with the types and properties of waves, cylindrical and spherical wave function and microwave networks.
The course introduces learners to the electromagnetic interference, conducted and radiated emission and susceptibility to determine electromagnetic compatibility.
Learners are introduced to monolithic microwave (mm) integrated circuits, various elements in passive circuits and semiconductor circuits.
It introduces to the components of a basic RF circuit, filter and biasing networks. It also teaches how to design a RF transistor amplifier and RF oscillators.
It deals with the numerical methods to solve electromagnetic problems such as Finite Difference Time Domain, Moments Method, Finite Element and Monte Carlo Method.
It consists of experiments such as designing a microstrip low pass filter, phase shifters, coupled line coupler, microstrip transistor oscillator etc.
This is an introductory course on satellite communication and earth satellites. It deals with the propagation on satellite-earth paths and types of satellite networks.
It introduces to the challenges faced in implementing MM-Wave, radio wave propagation of MM-Wave and the use of antennas and array for MM-Wave appliances.

It deals with the various materials used in microwave transmission and their characteristics. It also deals with the methods for characterisation of materials such as Reflection Method, Resonator Method, Resonant Perturbation Method and Planar-Circuit Method.

Candidates have to submit a thesis on any research topic related to the course justifying skills acquired during the programme. This is a compulsory course which candidates have to submit for successful completion of the course.
Electromagnetic and Microwave Applications of Metamaterials
The course deals with the introduction to metamaterials and their realisation through resonant and non-resonant approaches.
It provides insight to the radar systems and methods of detecting targets and integrating pulse. It also deals with the radar clutter and Doppler array
This course deals with the RF frequency and its response to MOSFET and the basic principles of RF design.
This course provides an overview on antennas and antenna arrays, various structures of arrays such as linear, planar or conformal and the application of ORAMA computer tool in creating arrays.
Candidates learn basics of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems and designing micro machined components.
It deals with the basic principles and components of microwave photonics and the limitations of signal processing through microwave photonics.
Learners understand the methods and techniques of classical optimisation and single-objective evolutionary optimisation.
It introduces the basic principles of sampling and aliasing and the application of data converters and analog and digital filters.

blocks.value: Top Entrance Exams for RF & Microwave Engineering

value: GATE - Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering is conducted for admissions to postgraduate and doctoral courses in top Indian Institute of Technology, National Institute of Technology and Indian Institute of Science. It is a national-level exam conducted on a rotational basis by various IITs. It is computer-based test which consists of questions from General Aptitude and subject chosen by the candidate.

SRMJEEE PG - SRM University, Chennai conducts Joint Engineering Entrance Exams for postgraduate courses. This is an online, computer-based test conducted in three phases. Candidates can also attempt mock test provided by the college website.

KIITEE - KIIT Institute of Engineering conducts KIITEE for admissions to M.Tech and Ph.D courses in RF and Microwave Engineering. Meritorious students who score well in the entrance are also given scholarships for pursuing course.

TS PGECET - Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University conducts Telengana State Post Graduate Engineering Common Entrance Test for admissions to M.Tech or M.E courses across all engineering sub-disciplines.

BITS HD - A world-class institution, Birla Institute of Technology and Science conducts national-level Higher Degree admission test for admissions to M.Tech course across its three campuses in Pilani, Hyderabad and Goa.
